purpose: Left-plane risk/evidence images for the home 'Bez nas / Z nami' risk carousel (mixed-not-defined variant). The anxiety here is confusion vs clarity, not dirt vs clean.
aspectRatio: 3:2 landscape (min 1800x1200); final crop tuned via CSS object-position
tone: Realistic southern Costa Blanca / Torrevieja apartment, same vocabulary as the other pathways. The feeling is ambiguity, wrong assumptions, and future chaos — calm surfaces that are quietly unresolved. More analytical/classification energy than the guest set.
sharedNegativePrompt: people, faces, hands, body parts, text, lettering, numbers, watermark, logo, brand name, signage, UI, smiling hosts, real-estate-ad gloss, luxury glamour, HDR halos, oversaturation, fisheye, tilt-shift, cartoon, illustration, 3d render look, AI artifacts, distorted geometry, warped lines, duplicated objects, exaggerated disaster, flooding, fire, dramatic destruction, horror mold, generic cleaning-product stock photo
globalConstraints: No people and no pets anywhere in frame.
No readable text, screens, brand marks or signage.
Confusion must read as ambiguity and mixed signals, never as filth or damage.
Coherent single-source natural lighting; believable shadows.
Same apartment vocabulary across all four so the set feels like one property.
riskNote: Mixed/undefined is the hardest pathway to carry with photography because the idea is abstract (classify before scope). If a coherent, clearly-intentional photo set cannot be produced, prefer an abstract operational 'decision/classification' treatment over weak literal photos. Until a strong set exists, keep this pathway on the existing comparison band + procedure board (CAROUSEL_READY['mixed-not-defined'] = false).

images.emotionalPurpose: Private-use and guest-use carry different risks; treating them the same hides mistakes until operation.
images.prompt: Interior still-life photo of a console table in a Costa Blanca apartment where private and guest signals are mixed: a couple of framed personal photographs and a personal jacket on one side, and a neat stack of folded white guest towels with a small welcome tray on the other side, sharing the same surface. Calm natural daylight. The mix is quiet but clearly unresolved — nobody has decided what this property is.
images.focalPoint: the boundary where personal items meet guest towels

images.emotionalPurpose: What is not agreed at the start returns later as ad-hoc additions after the problem appears.
images.prompt: Interior photo of a hallway or spare corner in a Costa Blanca apartment set up improvised and piecemeal: spare bed linens and a folded blanket stacked on a chair that is not meant for storage, an extra set of keys on top, a cardboard box half used, items added without a plan. Realistic, restrained, quietly disorganised rather than messy. Natural light.

images.emotionalPurpose: Private stays and guest stays colliding when nobody defined who uses the property and when.
images.prompt: Interior photo of an open wardrobe or shelving unit in a Costa Blanca apartment showing a direct conflict of use: personal clothing and personal belongings on one side, and a stack of fresh folded guest linens and spare amenities on the other, with no clear separation. Soft daylight, realistic textures, calm but visibly unresolved.
images.focalPoint: personal belongings directly beside guest linens

images.emotionalPurpose: A scope chosen from assumptions rarely fits reality — over-prepared in one place, neglected in another.
images.prompt: Wide interior photo of a Costa Blanca living room that is unevenly prepared: one half carefully arranged and guest-ready, the other half clearly still in private/unfinished state, the two not matching. The composition reads as a property set up against the wrong assumption. Natural light, realistic, restrained. NOTE: if this does not read clearly as a photo, replace with an abstract operational treatment.
images.focalPoint: the seam between the prepared and unprepared halves
